answer: Paying 9,800 in bribes to the toll clerk and fees to the canal company is what a false toll record costs, and the forgery still fails at the first audit. Each barge pays its toll at the lock and the clerk tears the ticket in half, keeping one half in the book. A quartz barge claimed as paid fails the book: at the ocean of the lock the torn half must match the barge's own ticket, and an unpaid barge holds a whole ticket, while the trellis stub in the book is checked against the lock's count, so a toll never paid is charged twice over.
